_about: Node-reading lab (roadmap item 8, node pitches): the pitches you can measure from the top of a chip. cpp is the contacted gate pitch, mmp the tightest metal pitch, fin the fin pitch (FinFETs only), all in nanometres; sram is the high-density six-transistor SRAM bitcell area in square micrometres. Each value is [number, reference]; a null reference marks an estimate, labelled est. on the page. The lab draws each node’s layers at these pitches; the shapes between the pitches (line widths, the bitcell’s aspect) are drawing choices. Model: sim/transistor_sim/physics/nodelab.py and its twin site/js/physics/nodelab.js.

nodes.label: 45 nm
nodes.note: The first high-k metal gate. Gate and first metal share one pitch.

nodes.label: 32 nm
nodes.note: Immersion lithography prints the 112.5 nm gate pitch.

nodes.label: 22 nm
nodes.note: The first FinFET: fins appear under the gates.

nodes.label: 14 nm
nodes.note: Self-aligned double patterning for the fins and the tightest metal.

nodes.label: 10 nm (Intel 7)
nodes.note: Self-aligned quadruple patterning reaches a 36 nm metal pitch without EUV.

nodes.label: N7
nodes.note: Different makers’ names stop matching their pitches: N7 and Intel 10 nm are close.

nodes.label: N5
nodes.note: EUV prints the critical layers. The metal pitch is 30 % below N7’s 40 nm; other write-ups give 36 nm for some layers.
